claims.text: The feedstock is FeCoNiCrAl high-entropy-alloy powder with a particle-size range of 15–45 μm.
The standard HVAF-i7 process with 15–45 μm feedstock produces acceptable coating quality but insufficient thickness.
Selecting an HVAF-i7 spray distance of approximately 300–350 mm will increase in-flight particle velocity.
Optimizing the HVAF-i7 nozzle configuration and particle velocity will overcome the coating-thickness limitation.
Higher in-flight particle velocity increases particle kinetic energy.
Higher particle kinetic energy improves particle impact, deformation, and splat formation on the substrate.
Increased particle velocity enhances particle flattening and bonding upon impact.
Enhanced particle flattening and bonding promote denser and thicker coating buildup.
Increasing particle velocity can increase coating thickness while retaining adherence and minimizing oxidation.
The optimized process will produce greater coating thickness than the standard HVAF-i7 baseline using 15–45 μm feedstock.
The thicker coating will maintain acceptable oxidation and adhesion.
The intervention will remain effective for deposition in internal diameters as small as 120 mm.
The intervention will remain effective during elevated-temperature bond-coat service.
The intervention will remain effective within the operational limits of the HVAF-i7 system.
Extreme parameter deviations or changes in feedstock size may alter the predicted outcome.

contradictions.description: The restricted geometry is described as an internal diameter of 120 mm in the conditions field but as a 120 mm outer diameter in the boundary field.
